props.caption: time scale: how fast the game's clock runs · 1 is normal

B03.visual_intent: A real render: a grey track with a teal marker that a script moves by delta (top), and below it a square pulsing on TIME. At about 25 percent of the beat the time scale drops to one half: the marker and the pulse both slow. At about 60 percent the tree is paused: the marker freezes and the pulse carries on. Labels 'time scale 0.5' then 'paused'. Caption: 'time scale: how fast the game's clock runs · 1 is normal'.
B03.motion_claim: Both things slow under the time scale; under the pause the marker freezes and the pulse keeps going.

show.event: marker slides and the square pulses at normal speed
time scale 0.5: marker and pulse slow together
paused: marker frozen, pulse still going

B03.runner_up: manim: two clocks, one at half rate
B03.why: A real run shows the two cases the sentence contrasts, in one take; a drawing of a frozen marker and a living pulse would be a claim, not a result.
B03.capture_spec: C03: evidence/planning-checks/scene-project/scenes/scene_c03_scale_pause.gd. A marker (a ColorRect moved by delta, 0.2 of the width per game second) on a grey track at y 0.28, and a 02-pulse square centred (0.50, 0.68), 0.34 of the height. Frame-counted events: time scale 0.5 from frame 84 (2.8 s) to 209, 1.0 from 210, paused from frame 228 (7.6 s) to the end. 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+. The controller runs while paused (process mode always); the marker is pausable.

B04.visual_intent: A horizontal clock bar labelled 'default limit: 3,600 s · one hour' with a terracotta marker that runs to the right end and wraps back to 0. Beneath it a zoom, labelled 'shown with the limit at 2 s so it fits on screen' (the measured check): time from 0 to 4 s, the wrap marked at 2 s and at 4 s. Two curves on it: the upper one (speed 1, two whole cycles in 2 s) carries on unbroken through each wrap; the lower one (speed 0.7, 1.4 cycles) snaps to a different height at each wrap, a vertical gap ringed in terracotta. Labels: 'a whole number of cycles: no jump' and 'any other: one jump'. Small grey credit: 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · limit set to 2 s · pulse change at the wrap: 4 steps against 44 (of 255)'.
B04.motion_claim: The marker runs to the end of the bar and wraps; in the zoom the upper curve carries on through the wrap unbroken while the lower curve snaps to a different height.

show.event: clock bar with its marker; the zoom with the two curves

B04.runner_up: capture: a real run with the limit set to two seconds
B04.why: The real wrap takes an hour; the drawing is of the measured two-second run, labelled as such, with both cases side by side and the measured numbers on it.

B05.visual_intent: Two horizontal rulers in seconds, one above the other. The top, labelled 'tick counter' (with the real call name in grey, Time.get_ticks_msec()), starts at 0 on the left. The bottom, labelled 'TIME', has its 0 a little to the right. Terracotta markers run along both at the same pace. A bracket between the two zeros reads 'about 0.25 s on this Mac'. A small cross over a subtraction sign between the two ruler labels lands on the words 'Do not'. Small grey credit: 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · three runs: 0.26, 0.29, 0.26 s'.
B05.motion_claim: Both markers move together, always a quarter second apart: the zeros never line up.

B06.visual_intent: The two rulers from the previous picture. B06.motion_claim: The bottom marker lags for a second and the bracket widens by exactly half a second, then stays.

props.code:
var age := 0.0

func _process(delta):
	age += delta
	material.set_shader_parameter("age", age)

B07.visual_intent: GDScript card at left (the age counter, five lines). At right a real render: the left square pulses on TIME; a second square is added late and starts its pulse from the beginning, out of step with the first. Labels 'TIME' under the left square and 'age' under the right. Caption: 'delta: seconds since the last frame'.
B07.motion_claim: The late square starts at the beginning of its own pulse while the first carries on, so the two are visibly out of step.

B07.why: Cause and effect together: the five lines on the left, and the out-of-step pulse they cause on the right. B01 showed the opposite, so the contrast is the point.
